strengths: The mean-point correspondence construction is a useful, original practical contribution to multiview geometry. It enables approximate pose estimation from four tracks using established five-point and P3P solvers, substantially simplifying implementation of a difficult geometric problem.

The empirical evaluation is extensive: 90,000 camera triplets across 18 scenes and three datasets, two RANSAC frameworks, synthetic geometry/noise experiments, and outlier tests. Supplementary evaluation using the maximum error across all three camera pairs strengthens confidence that the gains are not artifacts of the main metric.

The results demonstrate practical benefits against a strengthened baseline. In Table 3, 4p3v(M)+R+F+ENM achieves nearly identical PhotoTourism AUC@10 to 5pt+P3P+R+F+ENM (76.16 versus 76.20), while reducing runtime from 56.52 to 44.51 ms. The shifted-mean variant offers further accuracy improvements across all three datasets.

The ablations meaningfully examine refinement, filtering, early non-minimal refitting, shift magnitude, and RANSAC thresholds. Hyperparameters are selected on a held-out scene, and the manuscript provides implementation settings and links to code and data archives, supporting reproducibility.
weaknesses: The claim of the best speed–accuracy trade-off is incompletely established against the strongest baseline. Figure 4 omits the 5pt+P3P variants with refinement and filtering, although Table 2 shows these substantially improve the baseline. At the Table 3 operating point, the fully enhanced shifted-mean solver improves PhotoTourism AUC@10 from 76.20 to 77.14 over the fully enhanced baseline, but increases runtime from 56.52 to 112.60 ms. Matched-runtime curves for that baseline are needed to substantiate the stronger efficiency claim.

The HC timing comparison includes a consequential initialization choice. Section 8.3 reports approximately 45 ms to load its network/data once per RANSAC run, substantial relative to the reported 60–67 ms end-to-end times. Initialization could be amortized across triplets in deployment; the missing comparison limits conclusions about speed superiority over HC, although it does not affect the accuracy findings.

The theoretical support establishes a limited geometric bound rather than reliable pose recovery: Lemma 1 bounds the synthetic correspondence's epipolar error by the image triangle's radius, which can be large, without controlling pose error or refinement convergence. Figure 9 also shows approximation bias on noiseless inputs. The statement that ENM makes scene dependence negligible is consequently stronger than established for general camera configurations.

There is a localized reporting concern in Table 7: on Cambridge Landmarks, the M+R+F and M+R+F+ENM rows exactly duplicate all accuracy and runtime entries of their corresponding affine variants. These unexplained repetitions reduce confidence in those particular supplementary comparisons.
